Name: La Cova Fumada
Tips: NO SIGN on door. Cash only. Invented the Bomba. Hours: Mon-Wed 9:00-15:00, Thu-Fri 9:00-15:00 + 18:00-20:00, SATURDAY 9:00-13:00 ONLY, closed Sun. Our plan: Day 3 Option B, Fri Aug 28 - AT THE DOOR AT 18:15. The 18:00-20:00 evening service runs THURSDAYS AND FRIDAYS ONLY and they close at 20:00 regardless. This is the single best reason to run Option B on a Friday. Call +34 932 21 40 61 re August holiday days. Backup: Bar Jai-Ca 2 min away.

Name: Quimet & Quimet
Tips: CLOSED ALL AUGUST (staff holiday) — off this trip, keep for next visit. Normally Mon-Fri 12:00-16:00 + 18:00-22:30, closed Sun. Standing room only. Sardines+yogurt+honey montadito is unmissable.

Name: Cal Pep
Address: Pl. de les Olles 8 El Born
Tips: Sit at the bar not the dining room. No menu — chef decides. Hours: Mon 19:30-23:30, Tue-Fri 13:00-15:45 + 19:30-23:30, Sat 13:15-15:45 + 19:30-23:30, CLOSED SUN. Join the queue 15 min before opening. One of the most beloved restaurants in Barcelona.

Name: El Xampanyet
Address: C/ de la Montcada 22 El Born
Tips: One of Barcelona's oldest bodegas (1929). CLOSED FOR AUGUST BREAK — reportedly reopening ~Aug 24-25 2026, confirm at the window before queueing. Then Tue-Sat 12-16 + 19-23:30, closed Sun-Mon. House xampanyet cava + legendary anchovies. Opposite the Picasso Museum — a Day 3 Option B lunch candidate (Tue-Sat 12:00-16:00) if open.

Name: 7 Portes
Address: Pg. d'Isabel II 14 El Born waterfront
Tips: Barcelona institution since 1836. Open DAILY 13:00-01:00 kitchen non-stop. BOOK NOW for the Sun Aug 30 ~21:00 farewell dinner — August weekends fill weeks out. Order paella Parellada or arros negre. White-jacketed waiters.

Name: Carrer de Blai (pintxos street)
Tips: Best Basque-style pintxos in Barcelona. Go 18:00-20:00. Try Bar Blai 9 and Tasca el Corral. Kids pick their own from bar displays. Most fun cheap eating in city.

Name: Bar del Pla
Address: C/ de la Montcada 2 El Born
Tips: THE DAY 3 OPTION B LUNCH PICK, 14:00 - walk-in, arrive by 13:45 for the vault tables. Vaulted brick interior. Outstanding croquetes de pernil and patatas bravas. Quieter than nearby tourist spots. Great wine list. Go for lunch.

Name: La Pineda
Tips: Open since 1930 — utterly unchanged. Shelves of cured meats cheeses conservas. Wine poured from barrels. Almost no tourists know this place. Tiny — 10 people max.

Name: Bodega Quimet
Tips: Ancient barrels cured meats hanging ceiling. Open since 1920s. Go Sunday 12:00-14:00 for full local vermut ritual. Vermouth on tap + tinned conservas.

Name: Ciudad Condal
Tips: Always buzzing. No reservations — arrive at opening 13:00 or 20:00. Great patatas bravas croquetas gambas al ajillo. Reliable high-volume quality.

Name: Cervecería Catalana
Tips: Lively reliable tapas bar. Great croquetes de bacallà and pa amb tomàquet. Walk-in only — arrive at opening. Good for groups and families.

Name: Mauri Pastissería
Tips: Classic Catalan pastry institution since 1929. Belle-époque interior worth seeing. Order ensaïmada or croissant de mantequilla. Splurge once.

Name: Xurrería Laietana
Address: C/ de la Xucla 4 El Raval
Tips: Generations-old churros bar. Hot chocolate so thick you can stand a spoon in it. Go early morning — closes when sold out. Guaranteed hit with kids.

Name: Bar Calders
Tips: Best morning café in Sant Antoni. Pa amb tomàquet + café amb llet for breakfast. Doubles as excellent vermouth bar at midday. Beloved by locals.

Name: Quimet & Quimet
Tips: See above — listed twice for map visibility (Poble-sec). CLOSED ALL AUGUST — not available during our stay.

Name: Bar Marsella
Address: C/ de Sant Pau 65 El Raval
Tips: Operating since 1820 — oldest bar in Barcelona. Absinthe bar with dusty bottles and peeling mirrors. Hemingway drank here. No music no Wi-Fi. Time capsule.

Name: La Mar Salada
Address: Pg. de Joan de Borbó 58 Barceloneta
Tips: Day 3 Option B dinner alternative if you want the rice - book in the morning. Waterfront paella and fresh seafood. More intimate than 7 Portes. Easier to book. Good terrace.

Name: El Nacional
Tips: Four restaurants four bars under spectacular 19th-century industrial hall. Ideal for families — everyone picks what they want. Walk-in friendly even in August.

Name: Kaiku
Tips: Tiny local-favourite. Possibly best arros negre (squid ink rice) in Barcelona per local food writers. Lunch only. Book ahead — small room.

Name: La Pepita
Address: C/ del Comte Borrell 98 Sant Antoni
Tips: Gourmet bocadillos with creative fillings. Queue moves fast. Great quick lunch between sights. Sobrasada + honey + brie is outstanding.

Name: Bar del Convent
Tips: Hidden café in courtyard of 17th-century convent. Quiet shaded atmospheric. Completely tourist-free. Coffee + pastry in courtyard silence. Tue-Sun.

Name: Forn de Sant Jaume
Tips: Outstanding traditional Catalan pastry shop. Ensaïmada and coca de llardons (pork fat pastry — Catalan specialty). Go at 8am for fresh pastries.

Name: Morro Fi
Address: C/ del Consell de Cent 171 Eixample
Tips: Excellent craft vermouth selection and light tapas. Favourite of local food crowd. More modern than Bodega Quimet but equally good.

Name: Bodega Sepúlveda
Tips: Neighbourhood bodega beloved by locals completely off tourist map. Wine from barrels simple food old regulars. The kind of place you return to daily.

Name: Federal Café
Address: Pg. de Sant Antoni Abat 24 Sant Antoni Barcelona
Tips: Australian-owned specialty coffee and brunch spot in Sant Antoni — pioneer of Barcelona brunch culture. Eggs dishes, sourdough, excellent coffee. Arrive before 10am on weekends to avoid queues.

Name: La Barceloneta Restaurant
Address: Pg. Marítim de la Barceloneta Barceloneta Barcelona
Tips: Traditional chiringuito run by the same family for decades on the Barceloneta waterfront. Utterly authentic — grilled fish, cold beer, plastic chairs, sea air. Best for weekday lunch.

Name: Tickets
Tips: PERMANENTLY CLOSED. Albert Adrià's famous tapas bar shut in 2021; its successor Teatro Kitchen & Bar closed Dec 2025 too. Do not plan a visit. Adrià's current flagship is Enigma (book far ahead) if a gastro splurge ever returns to the plan.

Name: Parking Pizza
Tips: Gràcia neighbourhood pizza restaurant — thin-crust Neapolitan style, outstanding quality, completely non-tourist. Beloved local spot. Good for a relaxed family dinner. Can book or walk in on weeknights.

Name: Xuixo pastisseries — Carrer Nou / Rambla de la Llibertat (Girona)
Tips: THE Girona thing to eat. Xuixo (say SHOO-show) — fried sugar-crusted brioche cylinder filled with crema catalana. Invented in Girona. Stacked in every pastisseria window along Carrer Nou and the Rambla de la Llibertat arcades. Ask for one acabat de fer (just made) — cold ones are sad. One each, they are rich.

Name: Rocambolesc (Girona)
Tips: Jordi Roca's ice cream shop — same family as El Celler de Can Roca (3 Michelin stars, repeatedly ranked world's best restaurant). The cheap way to eat their cooking. Absurd toppings, kids love it. Mid-afternoon heat stop on the Girona day.

Name: Placa de la Independencia terraces (Girona)
Tips: Big arcaded square with shaded awnings across several restaurants — the easy lunch call with four people on the Girona day trip. Girona is Celler de Can Roca's home city; even ordinary places punch above their weight.

Name: Koy Shunka
Address: C/ d'en Copons 7 El Gòtic Barcelona
Tips: Barcelona's best Japanese restaurant, tucked behind the cathedral. Japanese chef, top-quality ingredients. Omakase or kaiseki menu. Book weeks ahead. Worth it for a blowout meal.

Name: Honest Greens
Tips: Fresh Mediterranean fast-casual with Spanish ingredients. Great for a quick nourishing lunch that everyone can agree on. Good option for the day after a heavy meal.

Name: DelaCrem
Tips: Cult artisan gelato near the centre — pistachio from Bronte and seasonal fruit sorbets. Family treat after a Gaudi morning. Note: Eixample location — a 20-min detour from the Gracia squares, pair with a Passeig de Gracia evening walk instead.

Name: Bar Jai-Ca
Tips: Barceloneta institution since 1955 — bombas, la raspa (crispy fried anchovy spines), calamari, tortilla. Open daily ~09:00-23:00. Day 3 Option B DINNER at ~20:45, and the standing backup if La Cova Fumada is closed or sold out (2 min away). Packs out after 17:00 — easy at noon.

Name: Gelaaati di Marco
Address: Carrer de la Llibreteria 7 El Gotic
Tips: Artisan gelato steps from Placa Sant Jaume in the Gothic Quarter. Open daily ~11:00-24:00; full flavour range ready from ~12:00. The cool-down stop on the Day 4 Gothic churches loop.

Name: Granja La Pallaresa
Tips: The Carrer de Petritxol granja institution since 1947 — thick xocolata amb xurros, marble tables, waistcoated waiters. Day 3 Option B breakfast, 09:00. Order the suis (chocolate topped with whipped cream) and share. Split morning/afternoon hours — go before ~10:30.

Name: Granja Dulcinea
Tips: The other classic granja on Petritxol (since 1941) — the Day 3 Option B breakfast backup if La Pallaresa is packed. Same ritual: thick hot chocolate, xurros, melindros for dunking.

Name: Los Tarantos
Tips: Barcelona's oldest tablao (1963). A straight 30-minute set of cante baile and guitar — no dinner no filler. Roughly hourly 19:30 20:30 21:30. The low-commitment option: half an hour and about €80 for four. Nothing booked — decide on the ground.

Name: Palau Dalmases
Tips: Flamenco in the candlelit baroque salon of a 17th-century palace. About 70 seats no stage — dancers within arm's reach. Shows roughly 18:00 19:30 21:30. Best fit: Day 3 Option B 21:30 - 3 min from the Picasso Museum and Santa Maria del Mar which are already on that day's route, and the only evening this trip with room for it.

Name: Tablao Cordobés
Tips: On La Rambla since 1970 in a Moorish-tiled room — Camarón Paco de Lucía and Antonio Gades all played it. The full tablao night at below-Madrid prices. Book direct on their site; the Rambla touts resell the same seats dearer.

Name: Tablao de Carmen
Address: Poble Espanyol Av. Francesc Ferrer i Guàrdia 13 08038 Barcelona (Montjuïc)
Tips: Named for Carmen Amaya the greatest bailaora of the 20th century who was born on Barceloneta beach. Ticket includes entry to Poble Espanyol. NOT ON THIS TRIP — its logic rode the Montjuïc-castle stop, which Day 5 (now Girona) no longer includes. Kept for reference.

Name: Palacio del Flamenco
Tips: The big theatre-format one — three shows a night roughly 17:30 19:45 21:30 and full dinner menus. Least intimate but easiest to book late. The Thursday fit: out of the Sagrada about 19:45 dinner 20:15 Metro to the 21:30.

Name: Gran Gala Flamenco (Palau de la Música)
Address: Palau de la Música Catalana C/ Palau de la Música 4-6 08003 Barcelona
Tips: Flamenco under Domènech i Montaner's inverted stained-glass dome — the only way inside the Palau without paying the €22 tour. Two sights on one ticket. WARNING: selected evenings only not nightly — check the calendar for Aug 26–30 before counting on it.

Name: 23 Robadors
Tips: The anti-tablao: a scruffy Raval bar where local artists play for a few euros. One late flamenco night a week (traditionally Wednesday) from about 22:30 — verify. NOT a family plan: late and in the one barrio flagged against after dark. Listed because it's the real thing.

Name: Bar La Plata
Address: Carrer de la Merce 28 08002 Barcelona Gothic Quarter
Tips: LOCALS PICK Open 1945 Still serves the same four tapas anchovies pescaito frito botifarra tomato salad Wine from three barrels in tiny glasses Mon-Sat 11:30-15:00 and 18:00-23:00 CLOSED SUNDAY Tables go early standing crowd spills onto the pavement

Name: Bodega La Palma
Address: Carrer de la Palma de Sant Just 7 08002 Barcelona Gothic Quarter
Tips: Old barrel bodega in the alleys south of the cathedral Young chefs took over and kept the room Tortilla croquetas bravas plus creative ones Book for weekends Sunday-open alternative to 7 Portes for the farewell

Name: Bodega La Peninsular
Tips: One of the few Barceloneta rooms still pointed at fresh fish rather than tourist paella High ceilings marble tables chalkboard that changes with the catch

Name: Koska Taberna
Tips: Highest rated bar on Carrer de Blai Only tortilla on the street locals treat as a reference Skip the display case and order hot raciones from the chalkboard behind the bar Start the Day 4 crawl here

Name: La Tasqueta de Blai
Tips: Volume champion of the street 50 plus pintxos colour coded toothpicks fast rotation Mini burgers quail egg over jamon Deafening and fun Second stop after Koska

Name: Blai 9
Tips: Blinis and crepes instead of baguette bases White plate 1 EUR black plate 1.50 EUR Cheapest stop on the strip

Name: Celler Cal Marino
Tips: Off the pintxo strip Wine and vermut from the barrel cured meats Where long-time Poble-sec locals drink Finish the Blai crawl here

Name: Bar Restaurante el Xuleto
Address: Eixample Dret about 10 min walk from Sagrada Familia Barcelona
Tips: NEAR HOTEL DEFAULT Days 2 and 3 Honest Catalan home cooking grilled meat Weekday set lunch around 12.90 EUR Neighbourhood room not a basilica feeder Go 13:30 for the menu or 20:30 for dinner

Name: La Bendita
Address: Carrer de Sardenya near Sagrada Familia Barcelona
Tips: Casual Catalan-Mediterranean 2 minutes from the hotel Open Sundays kitchen non-stop to midnight no booking needed Featured Day 5 farewell dinner pick alongside el Xuleto and Bodega La Palma

Name: Casa Amalia
Tips: Traditional Catalan off the Mercat de la Concepcio Seasonal card proper sit-down table for four Book ahead Verify Monday closure

Name: El Tastet de l Artur
Address: Eixample about 10 min from Sagrada Familia Barcelona
Tips: Humble family restaurant home style Catalan cooking No English signage The no reservation option near the hotel

Name: Santa Magdalena
Address: Carrer de Santa Magdalena 6 08012 Barcelona Gracia
Tips: Gracia neighbourhood dining room Croquetes de rostit canelons artichokes with romesco Also serves esmorzars de forquilla Booking advised small room

Name: Bodega Cal Pep Gracia
Tips: NOT the famous Born counter of the same name Old barrel bodega fifty years back in time vermouth conserves cheese and jamon Grazing rather than a hot meal

Name: La Vermuteria del Tano
Address: Carrer de Joan Blanques 17 08012 Barcelona Gracia
Tips: Very old school humble Gracia vermut bar Lhora del vermut the way the neighbourhood does it at half the Passeig de Gracia price

Name: La Pubilla
Address: Placa de la Llibertat 23 08012 Barcelona Gracia
Tips: Gracia classic opposite the Mercat de la Llibertat Market cooking three generous courses Also esmorzars de forquilla 8am to noon Book ahead fills fast

Name: Bartali Pizza Co.
Tips: DAY 5 GIRONA LUNCH - BOOKED 30-08-2026 14:00h, 4 people, SVYATOSLAV PODOLSKIY, table COMEDOR INTERIOR (indoor). Neapolitan style pizza, 4.8 stars over ~725 reviews, gluten-free bases available. SUNDAY HOURS ARE 13:00-15:30 ONLY so there is no second sitting. Call +34 972 21 09 91 if the day slips. Minutes downhill from the Sant Marti steps.

Name: Draps Girona
Address: Carrer de la Cort Reial 2 17004 Girona
Tips: Day 4 (Sat Aug 29) Girona lunch BACKUP. Well loved local room in the Barri Vell. Menu del dia with plenty of wine included but the menu del dia is usually weekday only. Two streets off Placa de la Independencia

Name: El Carrito Barri Vell
Tips: Argentine grill on a medieval lane Big plates of meat and chips very cheap completely local crowd Easy to walk past Packed by 22:00 Check Sunday hours
